articles.title: Blue Wave Sweep: What Does Democratic Shift Mean for Hollywood and the Media?
articles.content: The Democratic rout in the midterms was a referendum on President Trump, prices and the war in Iran. But it will have impacts that go well beyond the determinative issues — touching topics of key interest to Hollywood studios, broadcasters and their teams of government relations professionals. Here’s a quick rundown of some of the key open questions as Washington adjusts to a new, blue reality for the final two years of Trump. The bill is bipartisan — uniting Trump and Adam Schiff — so in theory, a looming change of party control shouldn’t affect it. articles.summary: Jana Hojdová wanted to ask the Oscar-winning cinematographer about his life. A pandemic lockdown and 650 hours of footage later, her documentary captures what it means for a legend to feel understood.
articles.content: Robert Richardson has spent decades answering questions about how he makes movies look the way they do . articles.title: ‘The Pitt’ and ‘ER’ Are Similar Enough to Allow Crichton Suit, Appeals Court Rules
articles.content: An appeals court ruled on Wednesday that “ The Pitt ” is similar enough to “ER” to allow Michael Crichton’s widow to pursue a lawsuit over the Emmy-winning show. In a unanimous opinion, a three-judge panel denied an appeal from Warner Bros. Television, which has argued that the two shows are unrelated. “There are clear and numerous similarities between ‘The Pitt’ and ‘ER,” the court ruled, citing the emergency room setting, the fast pace, the medical jargon, the graphic depictions of injuries, and a young, incompetent doctor fresh from medical school. “We find the details here suffice for a prima facie case.” Related Stories 'Married at First Sight' U.K. Canceled by Channel 4 Following Sexual Assault Allegations Disney+ Strikes Landmark Content Deal With U.K.'s Channel 4 That Streamer Says Is Among Its 'Most Significant' Globally The appeals court did dismiss a claim against key creators of the show — Noah Wyle , John Wells and R. Scott Gemmill — finding no evidence that they were aware they could be violating Crichton’s contractual rights. Crichton was a creator of “ER,” which was based on a 1974 script he wrote about his experiences as a medical student. His contract with Warner Bros. Television included a “frozen rights” provision blocking the studio from making any spinoffs or reboots without his approval. Sherri Crichton, his widow, filed the suit in August 2024, months before “The Pitt” debuted, alleging that Wells and Wyle had originally wanted to reboot “ER” and only changed course after failing to secure her permission. Warner Bros. has argued that “The Pitt” is a completely different show, and filed a motion to throw out the suit under California’s anti-SLAPP statute, which is meant to deter frivolous lawsuits that stymie free expression. articles.title: ‘Wildwood’ Director Travis Knight on How Live-Action Filmmaking Shaped His Stop-Motion Animated Adventure
articles.summary: Director Travis Knight tells IndieWire about bringing techniques he learned in live action to Laika's stop-motion epic adventure story.
articles.content: Many scenes in “ Wildwood ” are designed to look spectacular. Even if each frame weren’t already rendered with the meticulous detail and artistry of stop-motion animation , the Laika Studios film is full of complex, chaotic battle sequences, a forest writhing with eldritch magic, and giant eagles soaring through the sky. But some of the most technically challenging scenes, according to director Travis Knight , aren’t the ones that look the most majestic. They are — true to the spirit of the film and the lesson learned by its stubborn, caring protagonist Prue (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) — the simple magic of everyday life. Related Stories ‘Club Kid’ Review: Jordan Firstman’s Brazen, Funny, and Surprisingly Earnest Directing Debut Is a Wild Party Movie with Heart ‘Being Heumann’ Review: Siân Heder’s ‘CODA’ Follow-Up Is an Essential Biopic That’s Not Afraid to Have Some Fun In fact, Knight told IndieWire on an episode of the Filmmaker Toolkit podcast that one of the most challenging sequences in “Wildwood” was simply getting its hero from one end of her bedroom to the other. Laika prefers Canon cameras mounted on large motion-control rigs, which offer the flexibility needed to capture puppet movements adjusted one frame at a time. But when the camera moves, it also has to do so one painstaking frame at a time. Knight, who’s now directed live-action features “Bumblebee” and “Masters of the Universe” in addition to his Laika work on “Kubo and the Two Strings,” wanted “Wildwood” to have the same camera language as a live-action film. He wanted the intimacy and wordless visual storytelling of a camera tracking Prue as she huffs across her bedroom, where the camera movement helps us see the decor shift from the artifacts of a carefree kid to those of a more disaffected teen. “I still wanted it to feel like it was shot like a live-action film, with that kind of intimacy with the camera. But a camera on a motion-control rig is the size of a Ford F-150 in our [puppet-scale] world.

articles.summary: A Tony winner for "Stereophonic," a leading man thanks to "The Musical," and the kind of supporting star who makes everything better (like this week's "Being Heumann"), Brill tells IndieWire what real creative joy looks like.
articles.content: It’s all glamorous — chatting Tony wins and snagging leading roles in movies and sterling New York Times reviews — until your cat needs something. Fortunately, actor Will Brill knows a thing or two about balance, and managed to both a) charmingly answer our many varied queries about his wide-ranging career and b) attend to his yowling tabby’s needs while doing so. Brill is one of those actors you know , even if you don’t know him by name. One of the “oh, I love that guy!” kind of performers. The kind of performer who shows up and instantly makes things better, or brighter, or somehow richer. His credits are wide and deep — movies like “Caught Stealing” and “Test Pattern,” shows like “The OA” and “The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel,” theater like “Oklahoma” and “Stereophonic” — and things are only picking up for him. articles.title: ‘Beef’ Creator Lee Sung Jin Launches Lila Pictures, Developing Two Series For Netflix Including ‘The Only Child’ Limited Series With Ali Wong
articles.content: Six months after re-upping his overall deal with Netflix, Beef creator Lee Sung Jin has formed a new production company and has set two projects in development with the streamer. The series follows two longtime friends and neighbors whose obsession with solving a local crime becomes an escape from the private crises neither is ready to face. The season follows Lenni through a new case, where the stakes couldn’t be higher as her work and personal life collide. articles.title: Harold Greene Dies: Longtime L.A. News Anchor Was 82
articles.content: Harold Greene , the likeable longtime news anchor for many of L.A.’s local news stations, died last night. His passing was announced by family. Greene was 82. At various junctures in his career, Greene worked for ABC7 Eyewitness News, KCAL 9 News and CBS 2 News. Greene also worked in San Diego for a period, and legend has long had it that his on-air look at the time (including an impressive mustache) inspired elements of the Ron Burgundy character in Anchorman . Will Ferrell has denied this, however. Greene got his first job in L.A. as a reporter and producer for KABC. Shortly thereafter, he left for the San Diego affiliate, KCST-TV (now KNSD). He then jumped to the NBC affiliate at the time, KGTV, to co-anchor the news. In 1978, he co-anchored the news in L.A. with Eyewitness News legend Jerry Dunphy. He became ABC7’s weekend anchor with Joanne Ishimine in 1982 before taking over the anchor chair for the 4 p.m. and 6 p.m. weeknight editions of Eyewitness News after Dunphy left. He later moved to the 5 p.m. and 11 p.m. slots. At ABC, Greene also hosted locally produced light-news programs such as Hollywood Close-Up and A.M. Los Angeles . In 2001, he moved to CBS 2 and was part of a formidable on-air lineup that included L.A. TV News stalwarts Ann Martin and sportscaster Jim Hill. Later, Laura Diaz and weatherman Johnny Mountain joined the crew, reuniting members of KABC’s Eyewitness News team from the 1980s and early 1990s. Greene and Martin were laid off by KCBS/KCAL in 2008. Greene received 10 Golden Mike awards, the Columbia Graduate School of Journalism Award, two Emmys, three Edward R. Murrow Awards and twelve L.A. Based on an Australian format, the series sees experts match two single strangers who meet for the first time on their wedding day before immediately moving in together. articles.content: Inde Navarrette ‘s hot streak isn’t ending anytime soon. articles.title: ‘Fruitcakes: Dawn of Drag’ Goes Back to ‘Happy Gays,’ “Reclaiming History” Through a Timely Film (Exclusive Trailer and Chat)
articles.summary: Finnish filmmaker Vesa Kuosmanen discusses his doc, premiering at Tallinn, how it feels like a story for our time amid a backlash against trans and queer rights, and how fear drives anger.
articles.content: Happy Gays . That was the name of Finland’s first drag show in the late 1970s, which drew big, loud and proud audiences. Among the people on stage back then were Mummo, one of the first openly gay men in the country, and his best friend Jolanda. Now, you can relive, or experience for the first time, some of the excitement of those days in the new documentary Fruitcakes: Dawn of Drag , which will celebrate its world premiere during the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) in Estonia. But it isn’t all about fun and panache. After all, not everyone was happy to hear about the now-legendary drag show and its performers’ joy back in the day. And when the AIDS crisis hit, fear and violence were among the responses. In 1988, Mummo was killed in his home in Helsinki. Amid the more recent backlash against queer rights, he started thinking about making a film about that not-so-distant past. He met the aforementioned Jolanda, a retired archivist. More than 30 years after his friend’s death, Jolanda opened up his own archive for Fruitcakes: Dawn of Drag . And the filmmaker and Jolanda invited a new generation of drag artists to bring Happy Gays back to the stage. The heartwarming film takes us on a ride through archive and new footage and rehearsals and re-enactments of Happy Gays that bring up happy but also painful memories, along with a different side of the at times curmudgeonly Jolanda. articles.title: ‘Sounds of the Desert’ Explores Lives, Music and Cosmic Visions of Two Members of the Sun Ra Arkestra (Exclusive Tallinn Trailer)
articles.summary: “In a time of displacement and division, their music reminds me that we can still build a shelter together,” says Lithuanian filmmaker Emilija Škarnulytė, whose new doc premieres at Estonia’s Black Nights Film Festival.
articles.content: The lives, the music and the cosmic visions of two members of the Sun Ra Arkestra, one of jazz’s longest-running avant-garde ensembles, get a spotlight in a new documentary. Sounds of the Desert , the new film from Lithuanian writer, director, producer and artist Emilija Škarnulytė ( Burial ), follows Abshalom Ben Shlomo, who died in 2024, and Marshall Allen, who is still performing at age 102. The cinematic meditation on the avant-garde musicians unfolds through interviews, archival footage and live performance. To the sounds of the Sun Ra Arkestra’s music, the film travels through landscapes shaped by and tied to its sound, such as the Arkestral House of Sun Ra in Philadelphia, Chicago, a forest in Lithuania and the Negev Desert. Set to world premiere on Nov. 18 in the Rebels With a Cause Competition at the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF) in Estonia, Sounds of the Desert dives into the Arkestra, which was founded by Sun Ra in Chicago in the mid-1950s and brought together avant-garde music, cosmic philosophy, ritual and spectacle. The ensemble became a foundational influence on Afrofuturism and imagining outer space as a realm of Black freedom. articles.content: Nicolas Cage is endorsing Ryan Gosling ‘s upcoming take on Ghost Rider , nearly two decades after he played the character. Cage starred in 2007’s Ghost Rider , following motorcycle stuntman Johnny Blaze who sells his soul to become a bounty hunter of evil demons; he reprised the role in 2012 sequel Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance . articles.content: Dark Sky Films has acquired U.S. rights to American Dollhouse , the horror thriller from writer-director John Valley, and plans a theatrical release in January 2027. The film had its world premiere at SXSW earlier this year. Blue Finch Films, which handles international sales, has also closed Canada, selling to Vortex Media. The group will be shopping the title to buyers at the American Film Market in Los Angeles next week. American Dollhouse follows Sarah, who, after she inherits her childhood home, is stalked by a neighbor whose obsession with her turns violent. Hailley Lauren ( My Stretch of Texas Ground ) stars alongside Kelsey Pribilski ( Man Finds Tape ), Tinus Seaux, Danielle Evon Ploeger and Richard C. Jones. David Axe, Samuel Butler, Shane Greb and Roosevelt Film Lab’s Christian Sosa and Jon Wroblewski produced. Dark Sky, the genre label of Badie and Hamza Ali’s MPI Media Group, counts such horror classics as The Texas Chain Saw Massacre in its library, alongside in-house productions such as Ti West’s The House of the Devil and The Innkeepers , and horror comedies including Ted Geoghegan’s We Are Still Here and Ben Kitnick’s Let’s Start A Cult .

articles.content: Daisy Ridley , Sosie Bacon and Simon Rex are set to star in Get Rid of It , a horror project that Ry Russo-Young will direct from a script by Gemma Holdway. Production is scheduled to begin at the start of the first quarter of 2027. Ridley will play Harper, who discovers she is pregnant after a one-night stand with a drifter named Miller, played by Rex. Bacon will play Harper’s sister, Jessie. The sisters set out on a cross-country road trip and find themselves fighting for survival when they learn that what is growing inside Harper may not be human. articles.title: ‘Joy Will Prevail,’ Starring Griffin Dunne as Architect Louis Kahn and Alexis Bledel, Tells the Story of the Director’s Childhood Home (Exclusive PÖFF Trailer)
articles.summary: The feature debut of Max Korman, whose grandfather commissioned the architectural icon's final building, gets its international premiere at Tallinn, a nod to Kahn's birth in Estonia.
articles.content: Louis I. Kahn , just like the buildings he created, is an architectural icon. The Estonian-born American architect, based in Philadelphia, founded his own atelier in 1935. Among his famous, and often monumental and monolithic, buildings are Bangladesh’s Jatiyo Sangsad Bhaban, or National Assembly Building, the Kimbell Art Museum in Fort Worth, Texas and the Salk Institute for Biological Studies in La Jolla, California. Now, the final three years of his life and work get the big-screen treatment in Joy Will Prevail , directed by Max Korman, the grandson of Steve Korman, who, as the biographical drama shows, commissioned a house from the celebrated architect outside Philadelphia. The Korman House became the final residential building designed by Kahn. It was completed shortly before his unexpected death in 1974, and it became the director’s childhood home. The film also touches on how Kahn quietly navigated a complex personal life as the father of children with three different women. After its recent world premiere at the Philadelphia Film Festival, Joy Will Prevail , appropriately, gets its international premiere in Estonia, at the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ), on Saturday, Nov. 7. Griffin Dunne ( The French Dispatch , After Hours , An American Werewolf in London ) stars as Louis I. Kahn, with Jennifer Beals ( The L Word , NCIS: New York , Flashdance ) and Alexis Bledel ( The Handmaid’s Tale , Gilmore Girls ) adding further star power. articles.title: ‘Married at First Sight UK’ Canceled Amid Rape Claims, Review Finds “Pressure” on Contestants to Be Intimate
articles.summary: CEO Priya Dogra has decided that the "right course was to bring 'MAFS UK' on Channel 4 to an end."
articles.content: Channel 4 has been hit with a raft of recommendations to its Married at First Sight UK welfare procedures after two contestants claimed they had been raped during the filming of the show. In response, the U.K. broadcaster has canceled the show entirely. That decision was unveiled despite an external review giving the green light to produce future installments with improvements to the welfare framework. The suggestions for Channel 4 and production company CPL included installing CCTV, putting locks in shared bedrooms, and giving contestants access to a panic button. articles.title: TV Ratings: Blue Wave Fuels Surge in Midterm Election Night Viewing, NBC Leads Primetime
articles.summary: If the numbers hold, NBC will be the first broadcast network to win an election night in total viewers since 2012.
articles.content: A dominant showing by Democrats in the 2026 midterms also resulted in — at least for one night — a realignment in viewing of election night news coverage. Early data from Nielsen shows NBC leading primetime Tuesday night, by a wide enough margin that it will likely hold up through further adjustments to the ratings. That’s a big change from the 2022 midterms, when NBC finished fourth among the six most watched news outlets. NBC also claimed the most watched live stream of election night with its “Kornacki Cam,” focused solely on data analyst and video board operator Steve Kornacki. In the likely event the preliminary ratings carry through, NBC will be the first broadcast network to lead a federal election night in total viewers since the 2012 presidential election (also topped by NBC). Election coverage across outlets is already up compared to 2022, but it might not hit the historically high levels of the 2018 midterms . NBC averaged 6.8 million viewers in primetime, based on Nielsen fast national ratings, including out of home viewing. ABC finished second with 5.12 million viewers. The three largest cable news channels — CNN (4.159 million), MS NOW (4.156 million) and Fox News (4.04 million) — are currently within 120,000 viewers of one another. CBS is further back at 2.73 million viewers. The fast nationals don’t include Nielsen’s big data component, so the numbers are pretty likely to change some. NBC should hold onto its primetime lead, but the cable networks are so tightly bunched that the order could easily get mixed up. This story will be updated, including comparisons to networks’ performance four years ago, as more ratings data becomes available. The combined total of 27.05 million viewers across the six networks is already ahead of the final, 12-network total for the 2022 midterms of 25.43 million . articles.summary: The Broadway awards show has called the broadcast network home since 1978, for the past 48 years.
articles.content: The Broadway awards ceremony has inked a new deal to stay on the Skydance-owned network through 2032. Starting in 2021, the show began airing as two parts, with the first, largely made up of creative awards, streaming on Paramount-owned platforms. The Tonys has aired on CBS for 48 years, since 1978. articles.summary: The ‘Beverly Hills, 90210’ castmates have reunited in an ultrashort and star-driven thriller for vertTV that also features fellow former co-star Carol Potter, who played Cindy Walsh.
articles.content: Beverly Hills, 90210 stars Tori Spelling and Brian Austin Green have reunited in the scripted microdrama world. Spelling, who played Donna Martin in the original drama, and Green, who appeared as her onscreen love interest, David Silver, are both starring in an untitled original thriller microseries for vertTV, with production wrapping Wednesday in Los Angeles. The first vertical microseries for either of them also features 90210 alum Carol Potter, who played Cindy Walsh, the mom of twins Brenda (Shannen Doherty) and Brandon Walsh (Jason Priestley). articles.title: ‘Beef’ Creator Lee Sung Jin Launches Production Company, Plans Ali Wong Limited Series
articles.summary: Hyunji Ward will run Lee's Lila Pictures, which also has a Gene Hong drama series in development.
articles.content: On Wednesday, Lee revealed the launch of his new production company Lila Pictures , which has been formed to facilitate the creation of scripted series and feature films under Lee’s Netflix pact. Hyunji Ward ( Daddio ), who started her career at UTA and spent the past four years at Dakota Johnson’s TeaTime Pictures, will be Lila’s senior vice president of film and television. Lila (pronounced “Lee-lah”) Pictures derives its name from the Sanskrit word meaning “divine play.” So it’s pretty clever. Lee will use the banner to create, executive produce, write and direct series and films, while also “investing in the next generation of creative voices,” per the announcement. Related Stories Movies 'Street Fighter' Director Kitao Sakurai Built a Career by Embracing the Ridiculous TV David Harbour Thanks HBO for "Tons of Notes" as He Lands First Emmy Win Beef , a two-season anthology series, has won 11 Emmys out of 29 nominations. Lee was personally nominated for both writing and directing, becoming the first Asian creator to secure multiple Emmy nominations across writing, directing and producing categories for the same series. “I’m excited to launch Lila Pictures with the support of my creative home at Netflix and the help of Hyunji Ward,” Lee said, in part. “This is just the beginning. articles.title: Toni Collette to Lead Apple TV Dramedy ‘Lenni’
articles.summary: The show, from Made Up Stories and Keshet International, is based on a critically acclaimed Norwegian series.
articles.content: Apple TV ‘s latest series is going to opposite ends of the Earth for its inspiration and physical location. The streamer has picked up a dramedy called Lenni , with Toni Collette playing the title character. The series is based on a critically acclaimed Norwegian show, Pernille , and has started production in Australia, almost literally the other side of the world. In Lenni , Emmy winner Collette ( United States of Tara, Wayward ) will play a child welfare worker and divorced mother of two kids who “spends her days fighting for other people’s families while her own is in a constant state of hilarious chaos,” the logline reads. “The season follows Lenni through a new case, where the stakes couldn’t be higher as her work and personal life collides.” Related Stories TV 'Monarch: Legacy of Monsters' Eyes Season 3 Shakeup -- If It's Renewed Movies Ted McGinley Tapped to Narrate Volleyball Documentary 'Kings of the Beach' The cast also includes Ciarán Hinds, Dan Wyllie, Josh McKenzie, Celeste Barber, Genevieve Hegney, Arka Das and Wayne Blair. articles.content: Thaddea Graham, the actress from Northern Ireland known for her turns on Sex Education at Netflix and Bad Sisters and Margo’s Got Money Troubles at Apple TV, will be honored at the 21st annual Oscar Wilde Awards . Organized by the US-Ireland Alliance, the event is set for March 11 at the Ebell in Los Angeles in its traditional evening spot three days before the Academy Awards. It celebrates the work of those who are Irish — and some who are not — who contribute to film, television and music. Irish American actor Jack Reynor was announced last month as an honoree. Guests also will be treated to a performance by the Irish synth-pop singer Shobsy. articles.title: ‘Prep’ Series Based on Curtis Sittenfeld Bestseller a Go at Netflix
articles.summary: 'One Day' creator Nicole Taylor is the showrunner for the YA drama.
articles.content: Netflix is expanding its YA slate with a straight-to-series order for Prep , based on the best-selling novel by Curtis Sittenfeld. articles.content: “Evil Dead Wrath” filmmaker Francis Galluppi will helm the Hellblazer adaptation A new film starring fan-favorite horror character John Constantine is currently in the works at DC Studios, TheWrap has learned. This new feature will be helmed by Francis Galluppi, the filmmaker behind the upcoming seventh “Evil Dead” movie, “Evil Dead Wrath.” This film comes hot on the heels of “Clayface,” a film that proved that the DCU can support films of differing genres and budgets alongside massive blockbusters like 2025’s “Superman” (and its 2027 sequel “Man of Tomorrow”). “Clayface” held an R-rating and a modest budget, opening to a promising start of $43 million at the worldwide box office. John Constantine is a character who, like Clayface, can operate well in the horror genre — an element that’s been there since the character’s routes. The hard-edged paranormal investigator debuted in 1985’s “Swamp Thing #37” from Alan Moore, Stephen R. Bissette and John Totleben. Before breaking out into his own title, Constantine would go on to teach Swamp Thing about the more supernatural elements of his plant-based powers in Moore’s groundbreaking horror comic. The Hellblazer, as he was later known (including in DC’s iconic horror title “John Constantine, Hellblazer”), has already appeared on the screen a few times before. He was notably portrayed by Keanu Reeves in Francis Lawrence’s 2005 film “Constantine.” A potential sequel to that film was kicked around in the 2020s. Matt Ryan also portrayed the character on NBC’s “Constantine” series, later joining the CW’s DC superhero TV universe in “Legends of Tomorrow.”

articles.summary: Exclusive: The film follows the Oscar-nominated actor as he grapples with the death of his son.
articles.content: Freestyle Digital Media, the digital film distribution division of Byron Allen’s company Allen Media Group, has acquired VOD rights to the documentary feature “The Ballad of Lieutenant Dan.” The documentary follows Oscar-nominated and Emmy-winning actor Gary Sinise ‘s decades-long mission to honor America’s fighting men and women, support injured veterans, and stand beside Gold Star families. It’s a calling that was inspired by Sinise’s work playing a Vietnam vet in “Forrest Gump.” “The Ballad of Lieutenant Dan” will be available on North American digital HD internet, DVD, cable, and satellite platforms starting on November 10, 2026. It features interviews with Sinise, as well as Jay Leno, Tim Allen, Joe Mantegna, Chip Foose, and Mykelti Williamson. Sinise is also known for his work in films such as “Ransom” and “Apollo 13,” as well as the TV series “CSI: NY.” He starred in “George Wallace,” winning an Emmy. Related Stories ‘Wildwood’ Director Travis Knight on How Live-Action Filmmaking Shaped His Stop-Motion Animated Adventure ‘Club Kid’ Review: Jordan Firstman’s Brazen, Funny, and Surprisingly Earnest Directing Debut Is a Wild Party Movie with Heart The film also follows Sinise as he grapples with personal tragedy after his son, Mac, dies of cancer at the age of 33. The documentary looks at how Sinise is motivated by the credo: “We can always do a little more.” “The Ballad of Lieutentant Dan” was directed by Steve Mitchell Beebe and produced by Bud Brutsman. “’The Ballad of Lieutenant Dan’ looks into the world of actor and humanitarian, Gary Sinise, and explores how his commitment to veterans and first responders created a community that supported him through a difficult period in his life,” said Beebe. “This is a story about selfless kindness and, I hope, will inspire all of us to do what we each can to uplift our friends, neighbors and communities.” Freestyle Digital Media negotiated a deal to acquire the documentary directly with the filmmakers. articles.summary: The controversy-courting comedian/actor reinvents himself as a filmmaker, and as the star of his own hugely crowdpleasing movie as a washed-up New York party promoter forced to mature the hard way.
articles.content: [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on May 15, 2026 during the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. A24 will release “ Club Kid ” in theaters on Friday, November 6.] Ask any gay man with a social media account, and they likely have an opinion about Jordan Firstman . The backlash-courting queer actor/comedian, controversial most recently because of an online flare-up over querying the sexual realism of “Heated Rivalry,” is labeled either candid or confrontational. He also has a record of taking on sexually explicit projects like Sebastian Silva’s suicide-ideating, ketamine-fueled dark comedy “ Rotting in the Sun .” His status as a self-aware, hyper-online provocateur may not seem to suggest the makings of a bona fide filmmaker, but just wait. articles.title: ‘Being Heumann’ Review: Siân Heder’s ‘CODA’ Follow-Up Is an Essential Biopic That’s Not Afraid to Have Some Fun
articles.summary: Heder's look at a remarkable period in activist Judy Heumann's work is life-affirming in myriad ways, and boasts a star turn from Ruth Madeley.
articles.content: [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on September 10, 2026 during the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival. Apple will release the film in select theaters on Friday, November 6 and on Apple TV on Friday, November 13.] When Siân Heder’s “CODA” premiered at Sundance in 2021 (during the festival’s online-only “pandemic year” and months and months before the film would go on to win Best Picture), it became an early favorite of mine. Mostly, I wrote in my review , though the “drama is marked by familiar beats, its characters bring new dimension to a staid genre.” The same can be said about Heder’s follow-up feature, “Being Heumann,” which brings real life back to the biopic, not only through innumerable compelling characters, but the smart choice to tightly focus this story on one essential moment in the life of the activist Judy Heumann. articles.title: ‘Cherry & Virgin’ Review: A Fantastic Indie Anime Blends Different Art Styles and a Slew of Pop Culture References into an Innovative Modern Rom-Com
articles.summary: An erotic manga artist who's never had sex falls in love with a similarly inexperienced illustrator in Masanao Kawajiri's Tokyo International Film Festival standout.
articles.content: “I draw erotic manga but have never even held a woman’s hand,” admits Ryo (Takashi Okado) at the start of “Cherry & Virgin ,” a charming and cuttingly funny diagnosis of two lonely hearts and their mutual struggles with intimacy. He and the part-time fujoshi artist Ami (Yaeko Kiyose) have met on the apps, their feelings of isolation shown in the fact that they’re from different worlds — or so it appears on screen The most immediately striking element of director Masanao Kawajiri’s crowd-funded film — made with support from Toei, who are thanked in a winking moment that just about stays on the far side of the fourth wall) — is how the characters depicted in the style of art they are most closely associated with. Ryo is in sketchy but more naturalistic black and white and textured with screen-tone, resembling something like the more “realist” manga artists he name-checks, such as Inio Asano. Ami is shown in fully stylized color, illustrated in in closer proximity to the sort of BL (“boys love”) characters which she might draw and upload to Pixiv. articles.title: Alan Cumming Says ‘Tip Toe’ Was His Greatest Role Ever — but He Never Wants to Think About It Again
articles.summary: Series creator Russell T. Davies and Cumming tells IndieWire all about that devastating finale and why this role made the actor's career.
articles.content: [Editor’s note: The following interview contains spoilers for “ Tip Toe ,” including its finale.] Most viewers these days know Alan Cumming for hanging out with Traitors , in one of television’s most addictive reality shows. But recently, he took on a role of a lifetime in limited series “Tip Toe,” in which he plays Leo, a queer bartender with a heart of gold whose life is cut short when he tries to strike up a friendship with his volatile and bigoted neighbor, Clive. The five-episode limited series takes viewers on an emotional journey, opening with a shocking first scene which is also how the series ends. Leo has been hung outside his house, with Clive and a group of men looking on. Leo’s story is beautifully devastating, and the finale is one hour of gutting television. Related Stories ‘The Greatest’ Review: Amazon’s Handsome Muhammed Ali Biopic Connects in Spite of Itself The Mad (Color) Science Behind Rian Johnson’s New Camera App Cumming recently sat down with IndieWire to discuss the finale and why he now needs to let Leo go. Created and written by Russell T. Davies of “Doctor Who” fame, “Tip Toe” follows Leo and Clive (David Morrissey) in the days leading up to Leo’s brutal death at Clive’s hands. The show is not only filled with trauma, but deep joy, especially in showing the friendship between Leo and George, Clive’s teenage son, who is grappling with his own secret about his sexuality. Davies can’t say enough good things about Cumming, and revealed that he took the entire young cast to a Lady Gaga concert as a bonding experience. Cumming confessed that he and Davies had been trying to work together for years, but it never worked out timing wise, until “Tip Toe.” Let’s just say Davies had Cumming at hello. “Nine months before, we had a Zoom, and I simply described scene one of ‘Tip Toe,’ and from that moment on we had him,” Davies said, lighting up as he recalling the chat. He added that Cumming kept his schedule free a year before for filming the series.

articles.title: ‘Caligula’ Director Tinto Brass Dies at 93
articles.summary: The Italian filmmaker was best known for his hardcore portrait of the Roman emperor, but also made several notable erotic movies.
articles.content: Giovanni “Tinto” Brass, an avant-garde filmmaker best known for directing the X-rated historical epic “ Caligula ,” has died. He was 93 years old. His wife Caterina Varzi and children Bonifacio and Beatrice Brass told Italian news agency Ansa that Brass had died, but did not give a cause. Brass’ career kicked off in the 1960s and ’70s with a series of experimental films including his debut, “Who Works Is Lost,” which followed a day in the life of an unemployed designer. It screened at the 1963 Venice Film Festival. Other early works includes “Yankee,” a 1966 Western about a standoff between a bounty hunter and a crime boss, as well as “Col cuore in gola,” a 1967 murder mystery which featured Jean-Louis Trintignant. With 1976’s “Salon Kitty,” a historical drama set in a Berlin brothel during the Nazi era, Brass moved into erotic filmmaking. But it was “Caligula,” an infamous look at one of Rome’s most notorious emperors, that made a name for Brass. The film was written by Gore Vidal, who later disavowed it, and produced by Penthouse founder Bob Guccione. It featured a cast of esteemed actors such as Peter O’Toole, Helen Mirren, John Gielgud, and Malcolm McDowell in the title role, but made headlines for its frank look at ancient Rome’s sexual depravity, depicting orgies and hardcore sex. “Caligula” was re-edited and re-cut several times only to bomb at the box office when it opened in the U.S. in 1980. However, it has built up a significant cult following over the decades and an 178-minute “Ultimate Cut,” premiered at the Cannes Film Festival in 2023 to a warmer reception from reviewers. articles.title: ‘The Greatest’ Review: Amazon’s Handsome Muhammed Ali Biopic Connects in Spite of Itself
articles.summary: Produced in collaboration with the iconic athlete's estate, creator Ben Watkins' earnest eight-part series follows Ali from his Gold Medal win through his first championship belt.
articles.content: In 1977, just a year after “Rocky” reinvigorated the sport of boxing from the big screen, Columbia Pictures released “ The Greatest ,” a biography of the man who reinvigorated the sport in real life: Muhammed Ali , then 35 years old and still fighting, played himself in the movie, alongside venerated actors like Ernest Borgnine (as his trainer Angelo Dundee), James Earl Jones (as Malcolm X), and Robert Duvall (as fight promoter Bill McDonald). Fortifying the footage from his actual fights, they helped recreate his life as a professional fighter, from winning the gold medal at the 1960 Olympics through reclaiming the title belt from George Foreman in 1974. Lonnie Ali, Muhammed’s wife at the time of his passing, is an executive producer, as are Hollywood heavy-hitters Michael B. Jordan and Shawn “Jay-Z” Carter. Here, Ali is played by newcomer Jaalen Best, alongside notable names like Giovanni Ribisi (as Dundee), Dana Gourrier (as Ali’s mother Odessa), and Michael Ealy (as Malcolm X). The series starts in the same place as the film — the 1960 Olympics — and the first season wraps shortly after he claims the heavyweight title from Sonny Liston (Amin Joseph).
